summary: Built and ran the two registered probes in one fixed harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, reusing the repo's own test helpers) and recorded the outcomes, then requested formal execution of that same harness so the results rest on retained receipts instead of local feedback only. Campaign guard: a voter with entry 2 = EntryConfChangeV2, HardState.Commit=2 and Config.Applied=1 reports has_unapplied=true and stays StateFollower with 0 messages on both MsgHup and term-carrying MsgTimeoutNow; after raftLog.appliedTo(2,0) it campaigns (StateCandidate, term 2, MsgVote to voters [2,3]), and the control with a normal entry at index 2 and the same applied/committed gap campaigns immediately - so the suppression is keyed on the entry type in (applied, committed] and is transient, which refutes the stale-voter-set branch of that suspicion while leaving its bounded-liveness cost (a requested leadership transfer is refused until the application catches up) as the noted limit. ReadIndex: a leader that admits a read and then loses its term before any quorum ack drops that request with no completion (read_states=0, unconfirmed_reads=0), while a read admitted on the new leader is confirmed by one peer ack and delivered with an index equal to the commit index at admission - i.e. loss, not staleness, and that lossiness is already placed on the caller by the Node.ReadIndex contract. No defect is asserted for either question; both are recorded as source-explained negatives and the decisive readings (has_unapplied/applied/committed, vote targets, unconfirmed vs confirmed reads, ctx completions, read indices) are the operands a later interpretation will cite against the incoming CheckRun receipt. Still open: the receipt-backed successor interpretation, gap closures for both questions, and any independent sourced lead beyond these two mechanisms.
